newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thailand gives visa-free entry to future HK passport.
newsitem.headline: Thailand gives visa-free entry to future HK passport.

text.p: Thailand has agreed to grant visa-free access to holders of passports that Hong Kong will issue after the territory is handed back to China on July 1, the Hong Kong government said on Saturday.

The announcement was made by visiting Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasan, who met Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Anson Chan and future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Saturday, the government said in a statement.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, ending more than 150 years of British colonial administration.

So far, about 10 other countries -- including Britain, Singapore, Canada, and the Philippines -- have granted visa-free access to the passport that will be issued by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government that takes over in July.
Thailand is a popular destination for Hong Kong tourists and business travellers.
Hong Kong was also prepared to increase the length of the visa-free visit period for Thai visitors in the territory to one month from 14 days, the government statement said.
